subject.title: [Feature]: Support external unified session storage for stateless session mode

question: Should OpenClaw core pursue an external session-storage backend contract for stateless multi-instance deployments, fold this into the broader database-abstraction work, or explicitly keep session runtime state local-only for now?
rationale: The source evidence shows the feature is missing, but adding it changes core storage policy, config surface, dependency ownership, credentials, migrations, and session consistency semantics.

options.title: Keep This Design Tracker
options.body: Use this issue to decide the session-specific backend contract before any implementation PR is queued.

options.title: Fold Into Database Abstraction
options.body: Move the session-sharing requirement under the broader backend-neutral database design and close this only after that tracker explicitly owns session state.

options.title: Reject External Session Backends
options.body: Keep core session state local-only and document that multi-instance deployments must use a different architecture or future plugin/API work.

recommendation.title: Keep This Design Tracker
recommendation.body: Use this issue to decide the session-specific backend contract before any implementation PR is queued.

likelyOwner.reason: Current session storage blame and prior review routing both point to this handle as the best available owner for the product-direction decision.
